features.name: Hotel de Mores (Northern Pacific Hotel from 1885)
features.built_text: 1883, as a boarding house for up to 100 (HMdb); in use by Feb 1884 (Cow Boy); brick-veneered and reopened June 1, 1885
features.use: hotel, with livery stable and bar
features.evidence: Probably building "D" of the 1885 bird's-eye view, triangulated from SHSND 00042-00071 and 00042-00195; the reprojected base agrees with both photos (5 px and 2 px), and swapping D with D2 fails that test by about 60 px. Triangulated from two or more solved photos; sight lines cross within about 1-3 m, so the position is good to roughly +/-10 m once picking error is allowed for. Why the hotel: (1) a long two-story building with evenly spaced windows on both floors, the shape of the 1883 frame hotel (SHSND 00042-00149); (2) about 60 m north-east of the depot site - "a few steps from the depot" (Fitzgerald's ad, Cow Boy 1884); (3) long side facing north (HMdb 88037: "faced north"), with its west end on Main Street, which fits the race track running to "Main street opposite the Northern Pacific hotel" (Cow Boy) and the 1885 porch on the west side; (4) gone in the c.1905 postcard - the hotel burned in 1897. Further support (Oct 16): Houghton 3013534 and 3013559 (1895) label the long brick building with a taller gabled block at one end as the Hotel de Mores; building "D" seen from the east in 00042-00071 shows exactly such a tall gable at its east end. The Historic Medora marker for the hotel stands at Main Street and Pacific Avenue, about 20 m from this point (HMdb 88037; it shares a marker cluster, so this is weak support on its own). The high 1885 view Houghton 3013473 / SHSND 00042-00193 shows a large gabled building here too. Location raised to B.

Why Roberts Hall: two full stories about 80 ft long as scaled from the photo (the footprint uses the Cow Boy's 24 x 75) with few upper windows (a hall, not hotel rooms), a raised front on its south end, long axis north-south; still standing about 1905 (Roberts Hall stood until 1923, while the hotel burned in 1897); next to today's Old Town Hall Theater (Roberts Hall may be the "town hall" of a 1903 stereo, still to be checked); near the hotel and in view of the railroad (HMdb). Further support (Oct 16): Hagedorn's 1919 photo of "Bill Williams' saloon" (Houghton 3013539) shows a two-story frame hall with a fanlight in its front gable and a door to the upper floor; in his 1919 overview (Houghton 3013472) a dark two-story gabled building of that form, long axis north-south, stands south of the Rough Riders and north of the depot, which is where D2 is. The Roberts Hall marker (HMdb 88016) stands in a small park next to the Old Town Hall Theater, about 10 m from this point. Location raised to B; the Cow Boy's "lot 7, block 17" remains unexplained. Lot check (Oct 16): the triangulated position falls on today's lot 7 (parcel "7-8") of Block 13 - the same lot number the Cow Boy gives (Cow Boy 1884-06-26: "lot 7, block 17 ... in full view from the railroad"). Today's Block 17, in the southeast of town, is open sagebrush in the 1885 overview (SHSND 00042-00195), so the hall cannot have stood there. Either the 1883 plat numbered this block 17, or the paper misprinted 13 as 17. Neither block 13 nor block 17 is on the 1883 "Price of Lots" list (TRMF-01), so both were held back from public sale. The Historic Medora "Billings County Courthouse" panel shows a winter photo captioned "Roberts Hall housed the first county offices" (1886): a two-story front-gabled frame hall with an upper-floor door, the same form as Hagedorn's 1919 "Bill Williams' saloon".
